description: The bar chart compares the performance of various large language models (LLMs) on two mathematical reasoning benchmarks—MATH-500 and AIME24—highlighting how smaller models using test-time scaling (TTS) can outperform larger models using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. The chart is divided into six subplots: (a), (b), and (c) for MATH-500; (d), (e), and (f) for AIME24. Each subplot compares different model sizes and configurations, with performance measured as accuracy percentage (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 100). In subplot (a), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (78.2%) outperforms GPT-4o (74.6%) and Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (71.4%) on MATH-500. In (b), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B (91.6%) surpasses o1-preview (85.5%) and o1-mini (90.0%). In (c), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (95.2%) exceeds DeepSeek-R1 (97.3%) and o1 (94.8%). On AIME24, subplot (d) shows Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (30.0%) outperforming Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct (23.3%) and GPT-4o (9.3%). In (e), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B (63.3%) beats o1-preview (44.6%) and matches o1-mini (63.6%). In (f), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-7B (83.3%) surpasses DeepSeek-R1 (79.8%) and o1 (79.2%). The legend identifies each model by color and pattern, with TTS models (e.g., Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill variants) consistently achieving higher scores than their larger CoT counterparts, demonstrating the effectiveness of compute-optimal TTS strategies.
